client_stall_diagnosis.stage: between LWJGL backend initialization and OpenAL initialization; successful boots cover that gap in 5 to 9 seconds, stalled boots emit nothing further and die at the 180 second launch precheck
client_stall_diagnosis.root_cause: environment selection, not a code defect in the capture path
contributing_findings: operator-tools ships TWO Xvfb binaries with different SHA256: a binary-patched one in operator-tools/bin whose compiled-in XKB paths were rewritten to short stand-ins (/tmp/abc and /tmp/abcde/X11/xkb, chosen to fit the original byte length), and the unpatched distro build in operator-tools/root/usr/bin

there is no /usr/share/X11/xkb and no /usr/bin/xkbcomp on this host, and /usr/bin is not writable, so the unpatched binary cannot compile a keymap and dies with 'Failed to activate virtual core keyboard: 2'
the patched binary depends on /tmp stand-in paths, which are volatile and disappear when /tmp is cleaned; that volatility is why the failure was intermittent rather than reproducible
the home filesystem was at 116 MB free while the Minecraft client installation and caches live there
mechanical_repair: pin the operator-tools search order so the patched Xvfb is selected ahead of the distro build
pass -xkbdir explicitly to Xvfb from the qualified keymap data
re-establish the /tmp stand-in paths from the qualified operator-tools copies on every launch
pin Xvfb, xdpyinfo and xdotool by absolute path in the runner so the production path never resolves them from PATH
restore real headroom on the home filesystem

bounded_relaunch.retry_eligibility: only before startspec dispatch; a launch that never reaches the readiness gate has sent no startspec, armed no episode and captured no frame, so retrying is observationally identical to an operator re-running the entry point
bounded_relaunch.permanent_gate: startspec_dispatch_attempted is set immediately before the FIFO send and never cleared; _launch_with_bounded_retry refuses outright once it is set, so a trajectory failure can never be answered by relaunching underneath it
bounded_relaunch.stale_cleanup: stop_runtime, then pkill of the three launcher entry points plus KnotClient and fabric-server-launch, then Xvfb and openbox, then stale X lock and socket removal, then a settle delay
bounded_relaunch.identity_preserved: each attempt records the unchanged trajectory_spec_id, spec_hash and seed; no replacement identity is generated
bounded_relaunch.evidence: runtime_logs/pre_scientific_launch_attempts.jsonl, one fsynced record per attempt with outcome, stage, reason and elapsed seconds
bounded_relaunch.tests: tests/test_regime_a_bounded_relaunch.py: first-attempt success, failure then success, bound exhaustion, precheck failure sends no startspec, cleanup ordering, and startspec-failure never re-entering relaunch

temporal_alignment.acceptance_rule: each frame captured at or after its own tick and strictly before the NEXT recorded server tick, taken from the capture's own recorded timestamps; plus tick_queue_depth_at_capture equal to zero. No tuned tolerance.
temporal_alignment.large_lag_interpretation: Under lockstep a long capture does not desynchronize anything: the server holds the world until the acknowledgement arrives. The matching inter-tick gap for frame 0 is 4762.4 ms, i.e. the server waited. What matters is that no frame was captured after its successor tick was emitted, which held for all 260.
